findings.issue: The exact same architectural defect T-0635 fixes for agent-task (flowable:* stamped without a guaranteed xmlns:flowable declaration) is also present in lane-role-mapper.ts and timer-escalation-mapper.ts — both inject flowable:candidateGroups with zero namespace guarantee. WORSE than the pre-fix agent-task path: these two mappers still run and PERSIST their output at draft-save time (mapLanesToCandidateGroups/mapTimerEscalation are still called unconditionally in POST /api/process-defs, process-defs.ts:407-417) — T-0635 only relocated the agent-task transform to publish-time, it did not touch this. A diagram with a lane-assigned or timer-escalated userTask and NO agent task will still produce an unbound `flowable:` prefix on publish and hit AttributePrefixUnbound at Flowable's deploy-time SAX parser. Verified directly: lane-role-mapper.test.ts and timer-escalation-mapper.test.ts fixtures never assert xmlns:flowable is required/injected, and no call site invokes ensureFlowableNamespace for these two paths.
findings.suggestion: File an immediate follow-up task to (a) extend ensureFlowableNamespace (or an equivalent call) to the lane/timer draft-save path, and (b) decide whether lane/timer output should also move to publish-time-only like agent-task, closing the same draft-corruption risk class. Not blocking THIS task because: LIVE_PROOF T-0586 exercised only the agent path (author has not claimed lane/timer coverage), the gap pre-dates this diff (no regression introduced), it is explicitly flagged in pr-handoff open_questions with correct rationale, and T-0635's OTHER fix (BAD_BPMN vs ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE classification) actually improves the lane/timer failure mode today — an unbound-prefix lane-only publish now surfaces as honest 422 instead of false 503, which is strictly better than the pre-T-0635 state even though the root xmlns gap for that path remains.
